E1.evidence: Issue ros2/ros2#1341 gives a Dockerfile reproducer and the error `Unable to convert call argument to Python object (compile in debug mode for details)`; maintainer clalancette: "You are correct, it should work. And I confirmed it here; I'm seeing the same problem on Humble." (https://github.com/ros2/ros2/issues/1341#issuecomment-1303518557)

E2.evidence: The publisher (topic_statistics_demo process, whose rclcpp subscription topic statistics publish statistics_msgs/MetricsMessage on /statistics) sends StatisticDataPoint.data = NaN, which the definition allows ("A value of nan represents no data is available." in statistics_msgs/msg/StatisticDataPoint.msg). The consumer side (ros2 topic echo via rclpy, converting with the Python message classes generated by rosidl_generator_py 0.14.2) asserts `value >= -bound and value <= bound`, which is false for NaN. The failure depends on a value crossing the boundary (it does not occur with a peer that never publishes NaN), so it is not internal; the fix changes the generated code, not deployment wiring or build configuration.

E3.evidence: PAIR: the /statistics output of the demo feeds the input of `ros2 topic echo /statistics` (issue body steps 3-5).

E4.evidence:
Observed failure: "`ros2 topic echo /statistics` fails with the following error:

```
Unable to convert call argument to Python object (compile in debug mode for details)
```" (issue body).

failed_conditions.quote:
statistics include `NaN` data in the message, when it is being converted with `rosidl_python`, it detects the following.

```bash
Unable to convert call argument to Python object (compile in debug mode for details)
```

loudness_evidence:
The only diagnostic is a runtime conversion error raised while taking a message (fujitatomoya: "Error happens on the following." linking rclpy/src/rclpy/subscription.cpp#L135-L138 at 6e4d2ba2): "`ros2 topic echo /statistics` fails with the following error:

```
Unable to convert call argument to Python object (compile in debug mode for details)
```" (https://github.com/ros2/ros2/issues/1341). No build, connection, or activation diagnostic is reported; the reporter notes "At this point, `ros2 topic list` shows all the topics correctly, and echoing `/topic_statistics_chatter` is working, but echoing `/statistics` does not work."

resolution.summary: Backport rosidl_python #167/#182/#185 to humble (PR #188): the generated float/double setters use `not (value < -bound or value > bound) or math.isinf(value)`, so NaN (and Inf) pass the bounds check; message packages must be regenerated/rebuilt from source.
resolution.evidence: fujitatomoya: "using https://github.com/ros2/ros2/blob/humble/ros2.repos (https://github.com/ros2/ros2/commit/00f3ba9f73916a5eab322710edaaf197f0f10e31) + https://github.com/ros2/rosidl_python/tree/clalancette/humble-backport-nan-fixes, it works." (https://github.com/ros2/ros2/issues/1341#issuecomment-1306087432); reporter: "I just confirmed that the backports work when building humble from sources with @clalancette's PR." (https://github.com/ros2/ros2/issues/1341#issuecomment-1306798327). Both observations used the demos `humble` branch from ros2.repos rather than the reporter's rolling clone (77b75898), so the specified resolved composition was not itself shown; status is recommended with these observations as evidence.

notes: Class `other`: the definition declares NaN a legal value of StatisticDataPoint.data ("A value of nan represents no data is available."), and the consumer's generated setter rejects it (value-domain assumption, not a type, frame, unit, QoS, or encoding mismatch). One could instead read this as an internal defect of the generator; I judged it an interface failure because it is triggered only by a peer that publishes NaN. The consumer unit is named after rosidl_generator_py because that is the component whose revision the fix changes; the running consumer is `ros2 topic echo` (ros2cli ros2topic + rclpy humble binaries), and statistics_msgs (rcl_interfaces) must be regenerated with the fixed generator (clalancette: "the problem is in the code that is generated for the individual message files, so you basically need to rebuild everything from source."). The same generator fix addresses other reported compositions (ros2/rclpy#848, ros2/rosidl_python#162, #169), which are not part of this case. clalancette also reports that the problem does not occur on Rolling ("this seems to work just fine on Rolling"), where #167 had already landed.
